title: Secondary Sjögren Syndrome (sSS) in Rheumatoid Arthritis
summary: Secondary Sjögren syndrome is a common, often under-diagnosed autoimmune epithelitis occurring in the context of Rheumatoid Arthritis. It manifests as a keratoconjunctivitis sicca driven by lymphocytic infiltration of the lacrimal glands, requiring a precise multidisciplinary management approach.

sections.title: Definition & Epidemiology
sections.content: Secondary Sjögren Syndrome (sSS) is defined as the development of autoimmune exocrinopathy (dry eye, dry mouth) in patients with a pre-existing connective tissue disease, most commonly Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA). Prevalence of sSS in RA patients is estimated between 10-30%, significantly impacting quality of life and ocular surface health.

sections.title: Clinical Features
content: Ocular: Chronic burning, grittiness, foreign body sensation.
Oral: Xerostomia, dysphagia to dry foods.

sections.title: Red Flags: Severe Complications
content: Corneal melts or perforations due to extreme keratomalacia.
Development of B-cell MALT Lymphoma (increased risk in SS).
Severe filamentary keratitis impeding visual axis.

sections.title: Management Step-by-Step
content: Step 1: Patient education & environmental modification (humidifiers, eyelid hygiene).
Step 2: Preservative-free artificial tears (qid to hourly) and lubricating gels at night.
Step 3: Anti-inflammatory agents (Topical Cyclosporine 0.05% or Lifitegrast 5%).
Step 4: Punctal occlusion (collagen plugs for trial, then silicon).
Step 5: Systemic management of RA (DMARDs/Biologics) by Rheumatology.

content.explanation: S - Schirmer Test; T - Tear break-up time (TBUT); O - Ocular Surface Staining (Lissamine Green); R - Rose Bengal (optional); M - Mucin/Meibomian status.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always evaluate Meibomian Gland Dysfunction (MGD) concurrently.
RA patients on Plaquenil (Hydroxychloroquine) require baseline and annual fundus screening.
SS increases risk of corneal graft failure if transplant is indicated.
Don't rely solely on Schirmer's—OSS (staining) is a better functional marker.
